rationale: This is a one-term denominator tweak (dropping the cash subtraction) on the archive's existing SolvencyAdjustedProfit_x_EVYield with an identical moderator and identical economic story, i.e. a cosmetic re-parameterization rather than a substantively different mechanism, and the stated "diagnostic" value could be obtained more cleanly by winsorizing or flooring the EV denominator.

Capital intensity as the reason a pre-depreciation multiple misleads is an economically distinct moderator from the profitability-level, trend, volatility, solvency and accrual channels already tested, the expression matches the hypothesis and the sign discipline is clean, though dp/at is a noisy accounting proxy for maintenance capex (a capx- or ppent-based intensity measure would be a sharper test).

This is structurally the same short-side construction as the archived GlamourMultiple_x_ProfitFade with the multiple swapped from P/B to inverted cash-earnings yield and DELTA(MA) swapped for TREND, and the product of two non-negative ranks leaves the long (low-score) leg an uninterpretable mixture of cheap-improving, cheap-fading and expensive-improving firms, which is precisely the design that already produced a weak ls_talpha.

Testing whether the solvency and accrual-quality gates carry complementary rather than redundant information is a legitimate question that no single-moderator variant answers and the MIN conjunction is correctly specified, but it is an incremental stack of two archive components whose intersection will push coverage below 0.09 and risks an unstable portfolio rather than a genuinely new mechanism.

Recombining the own-history de-rating architecture with the best-performing solvency moderator and a cash-yield valuation state is a defensible levels-versus-own-norm test with genuinely lower HML loading, but both legs are non-negative so the low-score side conflates "expensive versus own history" with "weak interest cover," which will blunt the short leg exactly as in the generation-0 version.

The all-differences construction is genuinely new for this archive and the divergence story is coherent, but the reviewer's orthogonality claim is overstated: DELTA of a market-cap-scaled yield is dominated by the past-year price change, so the signal is close to a fundamental-trend-conditioned 12-month contrarian bet and must be diagnosed against momentum/reversal loadings before any alpha is credited to the divergence mechanism.
